articles.title: Secure OTP Generation and Validation — External SMS Evidence for Support Queues
articles.excerpt: Gate support-queue admission on a short-lived, single-use SMS OTP, and keep the verification decision separate from the routing decision. For a custom Node.js service, the deciding constraint is wheth…
articles.body: Gate support-queue admission on a short-lived, single-use SMS OTP, and keep the verification decision separate from the routing decision. For a custom Node.js service, the deciding constraint is whether you can explain why a contact-form submission entered a particular support queue, without treating a delivered text message as proof of identity or authorization. TL;DR: Generate the OTP with Node.js crypto, store a temporary challenge with expiration metadata, send through an external SMS API, and validate against that challenge before admitting the submission. Bind the challenge to the form submission and the intended action. Record the policy that selected the queue.

articles.title: JavaScript's \b Is ASCII-Only: How It Silently Broke Our Rules in Six Languages
articles.excerpt: We run a chat application used in nine languages, and a surprising amount of its behaviour depends on regular expressions: recognising that a user said "yes", detecting that a message asks for a photo…
articles.body: We run a chat application used in nine languages, and a surprising amount of its behaviour depends on regular expressions: recognising that a user said "yes", detecting that a message asks for a photo, catching a stated age in the safety layer. In one month we found the same defect three times, in three places, each time without an error, a log line or a failing test. A rule simply never fired. The cause: in JavaScript, \b does not know about Unicode. The behaviour A word boundary \b is a position between a character in [A-Za-z0-9_] and one that is not. That definition is fixed: the u and v flags do not change it. Every accented Latin letter, and every letter of every other script, counts as a non-word character. / \ b ( si | s ì ) \ b / i .

articles.title: Long-term memory for an AI companion without a vector database: 40 messages verbatim + 15 distilled facts
articles.excerpt: I run Lovora, an AI companion service for adults in nine languages. The number one thing people ask an AI companion is "will she remember me?", and "memory" turns out to mean two different things. Her…
articles.body: I run Lovora , an AI companion service for adults in nine languages. The number one thing people ask an AI companion is "will she remember me?", and "memory" turns out to mean two different things. Here is the design we use, and why. Two layers, two jobs 1. The recent conversation, word for word. On every reply the model receives the last 40 messages of the chat, both sides, exactly as written. In voice calls it is the last 24, because spoken turns need to be answered faster and the prompt has to stay small. This layer is what keeps a scene or an argument coherent. A summary would lose the exact wording, the jokes and the thing she promised two messages ago, which is exactly what people notice in a conversation. 2. Long-term facts about the user.

articles.title: How to Run Long-Running AI Agents in Production (2026): Runtime Limits, Durable State, and Surviving Restarts and Outages
articles.excerpt: Long-running AI agents need three things that serverless request handlers do not give them: a process with no short execution cap, state checkpointed outside the process so a restart resumes from the…
articles.body: Long-running AI agents need three things that serverless request handlers do not give them: a process with no short execution cap, state checkpointed outside the process so a restart resumes from the last step, and presence in more than one location so a provider outage does not stop the agent. Most teams find these gaps after a prototype works in development. In production it dies mid-run when a function times out at 15 minutes, a deploy kills the container, or a zone goes offline. Disclosure: Control Plane publishes this guide. TL;DR Long-running AI agents fail in production when the infrastructure treats them like short-lived request handlers. Common serverless functions cap a single invocation or request at 5 to 60 minutes, which ends agents mid-task.

articles.title: The Build Passed. He Still Owes the Explanation.
articles.excerpt: A finished check means the argument typechecks. It does not mean you understand it. Levent Alpöge says he and Claude formalized a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, without assumptions. He a…
articles.body: A finished check means the argument typechecks. It does not mean you understand it. Levent Alpöge says he and Claude formalized a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, without assumptions. He also says he has not mastered the mathematics sitting around that argument. He says the formalization is finished. Turning it into a huge document with sufficient detail is, in his account, routine. He amused himself and got past 250,000 pages. Claude called the pile a book. Theorem 1 opens by noting that the real numbers are totally ordered. If a number is not one half, it is bigger, or it is smaller. A checker will spend a page saying so. That is how you know a human never edited it for a reader. He did not post the pile. He says posting that unreadable dump would be inappropriate.

articles.body: Originally published at runheed.com . Returned with HTTP 400 (code -32000) by HTTP MCP servers built on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.x when a request's MCP-Protocol-Version header names a version the SDK does not know. SDK 1.32.2, the last 1.x release, supports 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05 and 2024-10-07. MCP 2026-07-28 is the first stateless revision: it drops the initialize handshake, so a client speaking it sends the version on every request, and the Python SDK 2.x lists it as its latest version.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.
